_note: The Gym manifest (WP25a): which grammar points act as selectable form categories, grouped into picker columns. 'point' must match the grammar point title exactly (resolved to ids at request time). 'usage' is the plain-language hover explanation; 'example' is a real drill sentence from that point. 'nonstandard': entries hidden behind the 'include non-standard words' toggle.

entries.label: Present
entries.usage: mi- plus the present stem plus -am, -i, -ad, -im, -id, -and.
entries.example: من می‌روم. — I go / I'm going.

entries.label: Negative present
entries.usage: nemi- straight onto the verb: nemidanam, nemikhaham.
entries.example: من نمی‌دانم. — I don't know.

entries.label: dashtan (to have)
entries.usage: The one common verb with no mi- in the present: daram, dari, darad.
entries.example: من یک کتاب دارم. — I have a book.

entries.label: Simple past
entries.usage: Past stem plus endings, and nothing at all in the third singular.
entries.example: من دیروز به مدرسه رفتم. — I went to school yesterday.

entries.label: Negative past
entries.usage: na- on the past form, never nemi-: naraftam, nadidam.
entries.example: من دیروز به مدرسه نرفتم. — I didn't go to school yesterday.

entries.label: Perfect
entries.usage: Participle in -e plus the short forms of "to be": rafte-am.
entries.example: من این فیلم را دیده‌ام. — I have seen this film.

entries.label: Habitual past
entries.usage: mi- on a past form: what used to happen or was happening.
entries.example: من هر روز به مدرسه می‌رفتم. — I used to go to school every day.

entries.label: Subjunctive
entries.usage: be- plus the present stem, no mi-: after khastan, bayad, shayad.
entries.example: می‌خواهم به خانه بروم. — I want to go home.

entries.label: Future
entries.usage: khaham/khahad plus the bare past stem — a written-register future.
entries.example: من فردا به تهران خواهم رفت. — I will go to Tehran tomorrow.

entries.label: Past perfect
entries.usage: Participle plus budam: the earlier of two past events.
entries.example: وقتی رسیدم، او رفته بود. — When I arrived, he had left.

entries.label: Passive
entries.usage: Participle plus shodan, normally with no agent named.
entries.example: این نامه دیروز نوشته شد. — This letter was written yesterday.

entries.label: Causatives
entries.usage: -andan makes someone do it: khandandan, resandan, fahmandan.
entries.example: او مرا به خانه رساند. — He took me home.

entries.label: Literary past
entries.usage: be- on a past verb and the particle hami — for reading older prose.
entries.example: شاه بگفت: چنین است. — The king said: it is so.

entries.label: budan (to be)
entries.usage: Saying what someone or something is: hastam, hasti, ast, hastim.
entries.example: من هستم. — I am.

entries.point: Two verb stems: present and past
entries.label: Verb stems
entries.usage: Every verb keeps two shapes: didam for the past, mibinam for now.
entries.example: دیروز او را دیدم. — I saw him yesterday.

entries.label: Ezafe
entries.usage: The unwritten -e that links a thing to its owner or adjective.
entries.example: این کتاب من است. — This is my book.

entries.label: Possessive endings
entries.usage: The owner hung on the noun: ketabam, madarat, esmash.
entries.example: کتابم روی میز است. — My book is on the table.

entries.label: Object clitics
entries.usage: The same endings on a VERB mean me/you/him, not my/your/his.
entries.example: دیروز دیدمش. — I saw him yesterday.

entries.label: Plural -ha
entries.usage: The all-purpose plural — and it is dropped after a number.
entries.example: کتاب ها. — books

entries.point: Ra marks a definite direct object
entries.label: Object marker ra
entries.usage: Postposed ra marks a definite object; an unmarked one is generic.
entries.example: کتاب را می‌خواهم. — I want the book.

entries.label: Comparison
entries.usage: -tar follows its noun, -tarin goes in front of it.
entries.example: تهران از اصفهان بزرگ‌تر است. — Tehran is bigger than Isfahan.

entries.label: Ezafe chains
entries.usage: Links stack, and only the last word is the real owner.
entries.example: در خانهٔ دوستم باز است. — My friend's house door is open.

entries.label: Numbers & ta
entries.usage: Counter ta between number and noun; the noun stays singular.
entries.example: من سه تا کتاب دارم. — I have three books.

entries.label: Broken plurals
entries.usage: Reshaped Arabic plurals in formal Persian: kotob, akhbar, olama.
entries.example: اخبار امروز مهم بود. — Today's news was important.

entries.label: Word order
entries.usage: Whatever else is in the sentence, the verb comes last.
entries.example: من چای می‌خواهم. — I want tea.

entries.point: Question words in a full sentence
entries.label: Question words
entries.usage: koja, ki, chera stay where the answer would; nothing moves.
entries.example: تو کجا می‌روی؟ — Where are you going?

entries.point: Light-verb compounds: kar kardan, harf zadan
entries.label: Light verbs
entries.usage: Noun plus kardan/zadan/dadan; only the light verb conjugates.
entries.example: من در تهران کار می‌کنم. — I work in Tehran.

entries.point: tavanestan: saying what you can do
entries.label: Can (tavanestan)
entries.usage: mitavanam plus a subjunctive — both verbs carry the person.
entries.example: من می‌توانم فارسی حرف بزنم. — I can speak Persian.

entries.label: Real conditionals
entries.usage: agar plus subjunctive, with an ordinary present in the result.
entries.example: اگر به تهران بروی، او را می‌بینی. — If you go to Tehran, you'll see him.

entries.label: Relative ke
entries.usage: ke covers who, which and that — and is never left out.
entries.example: کتابی که خواندم خوب بود. — The book I read was good.

entries.label: Infinitive as noun
entries.usage: raftan, khandan work as nouns, with ezafe, ra and prepositions.
entries.example: خواندن کتاب خوب است. — Reading books is good.

entries.label: ta (so that / until)
entries.usage: Subjunctive after ta means "so that"; an indicative means "until".
entries.example: به تهران رفتم تا او را ببینم. — I went to Tehran to see him.

entries.label: Reported speech
entries.usage: ke introduces the report and the original tense is kept.
entries.example: او گفت که می‌آید. — He said he was coming.

entries.label: Unreal conditionals
entries.usage: Habitual past in both halves: if I had…, I would…
entries.example: اگر پول داشتم، این خانه را می‌خریدم. — If I had money, I would buy this house.

entries.label: Written vs. spoken
entries.usage: miravam/miram, mikhaham/mikham, an/un — recognize both, write one.
entries.example: من فردا به خانه می‌روم. — I'm going home tomorrow.

entries.label: Formal register
entries.usage: gardid, namud, mibashad, jahat — the Persian of letters and forms.
entries.example: این نامه برای شما ارسال گردید. — This letter was sent to you.

entries.label: Adjective after noun
entries.usage: The describing word goes after the thing described: ketab-e khub.
entries.example: من یک دوست خوب دارم. — I have a good friend.

entries.point: Yes/no questions: same word order, just a question mark
entries.label: Yes/no questions
entries.usage: Leave the sentence exactly as it stands and add a question mark.
entries.example: تو می‌روی؟ — Are you going?

entries.label: Idioms
entries.usage: Set phrases whose parts do not add up: az dast dadan is "to lose".
entries.example: کتابم را از دست دادم. — I lost my book.

entries.label: Deference vs. intimacy
entries.usage: Choosing how respectful to sound: farmudid to an elder, gofti to a friend.
entries.example: شما دیروز چه فرمودید؟ — What did you say yesterday? (deferential)

entries.label: Classical verse
entries.usage: For reading poetry, where written bud is read bovad and means "is", and ze stands for az.
entries.example: توانا بود هر که دانا بود. — Whoever is wise is strong. (Ferdowsi)
